title: Alt-teksti: 3 virhettä
alt: 3 alt text mistakes and the fix.
Mistakes: no alt text, the file name IMG_2041.jpg, or just the word image.
Do this: Black wool coat, knee-length, double-breasted. Empty alt for decorative images.
How many of your images have no alt text? Save this post. Check your site at selkeo.com.
caption:
Three ways a product photo description goes wrong, and one formula that avoids all of them.

The mistakes are in the slides. Here is the formula.

For a product photo, write: color, material, what it is, and one detail a shopper would ask about.
“Black wool coat, knee-length, double-breasted.”

Keep it to one sentence. If an image is only decoration, leave its alt text empty so screen readers skip it.

title: Selittävä
alt: Accessibility basics: what is alt text, and why the images on your site need it.
Alt text is a picture described in words. A screen reader reads it out loud.
55,000 people in Finland are visually impaired. Some use the web with a screen reader.
Without alt text, a customer may hear “image”, “IMG_2041.jpg” or nothing at all.
The fix: open the image in your site editor, find the alt text field, write what it shows.
Are your images missing alt text? Save this post. Check your own site at selkeo.com.
caption:
There is a text on your website that most visitors never see, and some customers rely on.

It is called alt text: a short description attached to an image. A screen reader, software that reads a page out loud, speaks it to a customer who can’t see the picture.

Without it, they may hear a file name, or nothing.

In most site builders you can add it yourself. Open the image in your editor, find the “Alt text” field and write what the picture shows. One sentence is enough.

title: Arjen esimerkit
alt: Three everyday examples. Your lunch menu is an image. Not everyone can see it.
Lunch menu as an image: a screen reader may say lunch_week47.jpg. Fix: add it as text.
Product photo: a screen reader may say IMG_2041.jpg. Fix: alt text, Black wool coat.
Offer banner: a screen reader may say banner_final2.png. Fix: alt text, Winter coats 20% off.
Menu, product photo or offer: which one is on your website? Tell us in the comments.
caption:
Is your lunch menu a photo? Some customers can’t read it.

Text inside an image doesn’t reliably reach a screen reader, the software that reads a page out loud. The same goes for an offer banner, or a product photo with no description.

The slides show three everyday cases and a fix for each. Most of the time you can do it yourself in your site editor: type the text onto the page, or fill in the image’s “Alt text” field.

title: Tekninen
alt: The alt attribute: 4 cases, 4 right answers. WCAG 1.1.1, Level A.
Case 1, informative image: alt carries the same information as the image.
Case 2, decorative image: use an empty alt so screen readers skip it. Empty, not missing.
Case 3, image as a link: alt says where the link goes, for example Cart.
Case 4, text in an image: if it can be real text, make it text. WCAG 1.4.5, Level AA.
Automation finds missing alt text, not bad alt text. That takes a human. Save this post.
caption:
Developers: an empty alt and a missing alt are not the same thing.

alt="" tells a screen reader to skip a decorative image. Leave the attribute out, and it may read the file name instead.

The slides cover four cases under WCAG 1.1.1 (Level A): informative images, decorative images, linked images and text in images.

One thing automated checks won’t tell you is whether the alt text is any good. They find the missing ones. Quality takes a human in code review.

title: Myytti ja fakta
alt: Myth: alt text is just for search engines. Fact: it’s for people who can’t see the image.
caption:
Alt text is not an SEO trick. It is how some customers learn what is in your photos.

A screen reader reads the alt text out loud when someone can’t see the image. That is its first job.

Search is the bonus: Google also uses alt text to understand what an image shows. One good sentence does both jobs.

So write it for the customer first. If it would help a person choose, it is good alt text.

What did you think alt text was for? Tell us in the comments.

title: Kontrasti näytettynä
alt: Low-contrast text at 2.0:1 next to clear text at 17.6:1. The minimum for normal text is 4.5:1.
caption:
Light grey text on white looks elegant. For visitors with low vision it can be very hard to read.

Low-contrast text was the most common error WebAIM found on the top one million home pages in 2026: 83.9% of them had it.

The benchmark for normal text is a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 (WCAG 1.4.3, Level AA). A free online contrast checker gives you the ratio from two color codes.

The fix is often a single color code in your site’s theme.

title: Tarkistuslista
alt: Alt text checklist with five points. The full list is written out in the caption.
caption:
Five checks for every image on your website before you hit publish.

Here is the list as text, so you can copy it:

1. Every image that carries information has alt text
2. Decorative images have an empty alt, so screen readers skip them
3. A linked image’s alt says where the link goes
4. Text is on the page as text, not inside an image
5. The alt doesn’t start with “image of”. The screen reader already says that

title: Sanasto
alt: Glossary: alt text. A picture described in words, read out loud by a screen reader.
caption:
Accessibility words in plain English. First up: alt text.

“Alt” is short for “alternative”. It is the text alternative to an image: a short description that a screen reader reads out loud, and that shows up if the image fails to load.

You add it in your site editor, in the image’s “Alt text” field.

title: Yleisimmät virheet
alt: Bar chart of the six most common accessibility errors. The numbers are in the caption.
caption:
The same six accessibility errors turn up again and again on the web’s biggest home pages.

WebAIM tests the top one million home pages every year. In 2026 it found errors on 95.9% of them. The six most common, as text:

1. Low-contrast text: 83.9%
2. Images missing alt text: 53.1%
3. Form fields without a label: 51%
4. Empty links: 46.3%
5. Empty buttons: 30.6%
6. Page language not set: 13.5%

Automated checks catch all six, so you don’t have to hunt for them by hand. They don’t catch everything: whether an image description is actually helpful still takes a person.

title: Mikroyritys
alt: Fewer than 10 employees and €2M or less? The Accessibility Act most likely doesn’t apply.
caption:
Running a small business and worried about the European Accessibility Act? You may be exempt.

The Act leaves out microenterprises that provide services. That means fewer than 10 employees, and an annual turnover or balance sheet total of €2M or less. You need to meet both the headcount limit and the money limit.

This is a quick guide, not legal advice. If you are close to the limits, check with your national authority.

Exempt or not, the same fixes make your website easier to use for every customer.
